mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate at the zero bound (0.08%) has historically been associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.1% (p-value < 0.05 for the positive return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 235.0 (the 2013-07 vintage value of 232.9 is below this threshold), it signals accelerating inflation, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0 (p-value < 0.05 for the negative return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) are rising above the 2013-08 vintage value of 409691.0 and the federal funds rate is at or below 0.1%, it signals strong consumer demand supported by accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS > 409691.0 AND FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% (p-value < 0.05 for the positive return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is likely to implement accommodative monetary policy to stimulate the economy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 7.0% (p-value < 0.05 for the positive return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: The housing starts series (HOUST) at 880.0 (2013-07 vintage) has historically been associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as rising housing activity signals a strengthening economy and increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST is at or above 880.0 (p-value < 0.05 for the positive return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 98.0 (the 2013-07 vintage value of 99.0814), it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to recession fears.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 98.0 (p-value < 0.05 for the negative return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) are rising above 880.0 (2013-07 vintage) and industrial production (INDPRO) is falling below 98.0 (2013-07 vintage), it signals a weakening economy with falling manufacturing output and rising housing activity, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 880.0 AND INDPRO < 98.0 (p-value < 0.05 for the negative return rate being significantly above 50%).

mechanism_narrative: In monetary policy tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher interest rates reduce equity valuations and increase borrowing costs for corporations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (p-value < 0.05 for the negative return rate being significantly above 50%).
